messages.content: With Tucson settled, I need to start the Portland regional water-ops expo. First pass only, no booking. I need Bay Area to Portland flights for Monday afternoon, hotel comparison, and no rental car unless it really helps. Booth material check-in is Monday evening, and I have a Wednesday 9:00 a.m. technical session.
Got it. Is the expo at the Oregon Convention Center, and are SFO and OAK both acceptable? Also, is the Thursday customer dinner still uncertain for the return date?
Yes, Oregon Convention Center. SFO or OAK are both fine; SJC only if it is clearly better. Thursday dinner is only possible right now, so don't assume a Thursday return.

Here is the clean first pass. Flight best fit: Alaska SFO-PDX nonstop, Monday 2:15 p.m.-3:58 p.m., about $238 economy. It gives you time to get to the convention area before booth check-in. Acceptable backup: Southwest OAK-PDX nonstop, 3:45 p.m.-5:30 p.m., about $226, but it is tighter and seating is less controlled. United option: SFO-DEN-PDX, 1:05 p.m.-6:42 p.m., about $312; one connection is manageable, but it lands late for check-in.
Booth check-in is 5:30 to 7:30. I do not want to be arriving at the table at 7:15. Is that United connection actually comfortable?

The Denver connection is about 65 minutes, so the transfer itself is acceptable. The problem is the arrival time: any delay puts the Monday check-in at risk. For this trip, the Alaska nonstop is the better fit even though it is not United.
Agreed. Keep the Alaska SFO nonstop as the lead. I don't need United just for the sake of it.
Saved as the lead: Alaska SFO-PDX, 2:15 p.m.-3:58 p.m. Monday. With a rideshare or MAX from PDX, you should be in the convention area around 4:45 to 5:05 if baggage is straightforward.
Hotel side: compare the official block to the better-rated place nearby. I care about guest feedback more than being one block closer, but I still need the Wednesday morning to be easy.

Official block: Lloyd Convention Hotel, about a 2-minute walk to the hall, $239/night, guest rating showing around 3.8/5 with mixed notes on noise and elevators. Nearby better-rated option: Hotel Eastlund, about a 6- to 8-minute walk, $254/night, around 4.4/5, quieter-room inventory showing, and better nearby restaurant choices. For a 9:00 a.m. session, Eastlund is still practical.
What changes if the Thursday dinner is near the waterfront?

Not much on the hotel choice. From Eastlund, the waterfront dinner area is roughly 10 to 15 minutes by rideshare, or MAX plus a short walk. The official block is similar. I would skip the rental car unless you add an offsite customer visit; parking would be more hassle than value.
Ok. Do not book. Save Alaska as lead, Eastlund as lead, official block as backup. Open items are Thursday teardown and whether that customer dinner becomes real.

Saved, not booked. Best fit is Alaska SFO-PDX Monday afternoon plus Hotel Eastlund near the convention center. Acceptable backup is the official block if proximity beats the review tradeoff or Eastlund rate changes. No rental car planned. Open items: Thursday booth teardown, Thursday customer dinner, and the return day/time.

messages.content: Portland update. The organizer moved my technical session to Wednesday at 7:45 a.m., and the distributor dinner Thursday near the waterfront is now firm. Hotel block deadline is tomorrow. I still don't know if Maya can take Thursday booth teardown.

The earlier Wednesday session makes a quiet, predictable hotel more important, but it does not change the outbound much. The Monday Alaska nonstop still protects booth check-in best: SFO-PDX 2:15 p.m.-3:58 p.m. The United one-stop still arrives around 6:42 p.m.; the Denver layover is workable, but the arrival is too late to be the lead.
For 7:45, I care more about sleep and not fighting elevators than shaving off two blocks. Does Eastlund have anything away from the train side?

Yes. Eastlund is showing king rooms where we can request upper floor, away from elevator, and away from the MAX-facing side. It is not guaranteed, but it is a better request path than the official block, where the remaining block rooms look more generic.
Remind me of the hotel tradeoff now that dinner is firm.

Official block: closest walk, about 2 minutes, $239/night, but uneven guest feedback and less room-control detail. Eastlund: about 6 to 8 minutes to the hall, $254 to $259/night depending on rate, stronger reviews, better quiet-room request options, and easier restaurant access before and after the waterfront dinner. For the 7:45 session, you would leave around 7:05 and still have cushion.
Is the Eastlund rate refundable? If I have to fly home late Thursday, I do not want to be locked into the extra night.

The refundable Eastlund rate can still be changed before the cutoff shown for the reservation. Best move would be to reserve through Friday checkout only if Maya covers teardown; otherwise book Monday through Thursday checkout and use the late Thursday flight after dinner. The official block is less flexible after tomorrow.
Show the return choices both ways.

If Maya covers teardown: Friday morning options are Alaska PDX-SFO 8:35 a.m.-10:25 a.m., about $211, or United PDX-SFO 9:50 a.m.-11:40 a.m., about $236. If you must handle teardown and still attend the dinner: late Thursday Alaska PDX-SFO 10:15 p.m.-11:59 p.m. is the cleanest nonstop. The late United choices add a connection or arrive after 1:00 a.m.
Would the Friday United nonstop be reasonable? It is later, but not bad.

Yes. Alaska is cheaper and gets you home earlier. United gives you a calmer Friday morning after the waterfront dinner and still gets you back before noon. I would use Alaska for the outbound and United for the Friday return if teardown is covered.
Tentatively use that. Alaska outbound, Eastlund, Friday morning United return if Maya covers teardown. If she can't, late Thursday Alaska return after dinner. Still don't book until I get her answer.

Tentative plan saved, not booked: Alaska SFO-PDX Monday 2:15 p.m.-3:58 p.m.; Hotel Eastlund with quiet-room request; Friday United PDX-SFO 9:50 a.m.-11:40 a.m. if Maya covers teardown. Backup: late Thursday Alaska PDX-SFO 10:15 p.m.-11:59 p.m. after dinner. I would choose Eastlund before the block deadline unless the rate changes materially.

messages.content: Portland is confirmed. Maya has Thursday booth teardown. Book the Alaska outbound, Eastlund through Friday checkout, and the Friday morning return. No rental car.

Yes, use the United return. I want breakfast and some cushion after the Thursday dinner. Economy is fine.
Understood. For Eastlund, I can book the refundable king and add a quiet-room request. Any specific room notes?
Quiet king if available, away from elevator or MAX side. Add a mini-fridge request too. If the coffee maker is already listed, no separate note.
Got it. Seat selection is available on both flights. Should I pick windows if open, or leave seats unassigned?
Pick windows if they are available. Go ahead and book.

Booked. Alaska SFO-PDX Monday 2:15 p.m.-3:58 p.m., economy, seat 12A. United PDX-SFO Friday 9:50 a.m.-11:40 a.m., economy, seat 14A. Hotel Eastlund is booked Monday through Friday checkout on the refundable king rate, with quiet/upper-floor away-from-elevator/MAX request and mini-fridge note; coffee maker is listed. No rental car. Plan is MAX or rideshare from PDX, booth material check-in Monday evening, Wednesday 7:45 a.m. technical session, and Thursday waterfront dinner.
